dossier.public_summary: The dip depth changes dramatically from sector to sector and from transit to transit, with the whole signal driven by two unusually deep events on a highly spotted star. The 11.7-day period coincides with the star's 11.2-day spin period and huge spot modulation, making spot-driven variability the better explanation than a 2.3-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Depth varies by factor ~8 between sectors (sector 18 1324 +/-102 ppm vs sector 58 166 +/-89 ppm vs sector 85 473 +/-140 ppm), inconsistent with a constant planet transit.

Individual transit depths are not consistent (chi2=76.5 dof=5); the two deepest events carry share_of_top_3=0.965 with a 5.1 sigma deep outlier at -93 and a -4.7 sigma shallow outlier at -1, indicating a few bad events, not a steady transit.

Signal period is essentially the stellar rotation period with high-amplitude spot variability in sectors 18 (1698 ppm), 58 (4114 ppm) and 85 (16561 ppm); phase_curve amplitude 69.14 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.09314) and VARIABLE flag support modulation rather than a planet transit, though V_sigma=-2.266 flat bottom cannot alone confirm a planet when blend/variability explanations exist.
